transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Thompson, thank you for sitting down with me. I need to talk to you about something that happened during the monitoring of your granddaughter's baby.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What is it? Is the baby alright?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is doing well now, but I made a mistake. I reviewed the heart rate tracing earlier and I categorised it incorrectly. That means I missed some signs that the baby was struggling.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean? You missed something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. There were drops in the heart rate called decelerations. I told the team they were normal, but they weren't. A second doctor looked at it two hours later and saw that the baby was actually in distress. I am very sorry. This was my error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Two hours? You left a baby in danger for two hours because you didn't know how to read a chart?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I did. I was responsible for that review and I got it wrong. I apologize for that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is outrageous! Who is running this place? You're a doctor, aren't you? You're supposed to be the expert!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're angry, Mr. Thompson.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Angry? I'm bloody furious! My great-grandchild could have been killed because you were careless! How can you just sit there and say you're sorry?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is an unacceptable mistake. I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. I trusted you people. Now tell me, why did it take another doctor to find it? Were you just guessing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, I was reviewing the data, but I misinterpreted the patterns in the heart rate. I missed the severity of the drops. Does that make sense so far, or can I explain that part differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense that you failed. It doesn't make sense why you were allowed to do it!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how frightening this is for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frightening? It's a miracle the baby is okay! You're just giving me these fancy words.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. I'm sorry. Look, I have to check on a few other things quickly, but I want to make sure we get your questions answered.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You have to go? You're leaving now? After telling me you messed up my family's baby?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just need a moment to coordinate with the senior consultant, but I will be right back.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No! You stay right here! I want to know exactly what happens now. What are you doing to make sure this doesn't happen to someone else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm going to file a formal incident report today. We will also have a peer review of my charting for the last month to see where the gap in my training is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What about the baby? Is the baby actually fine or are you just saying that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is stable now. The plan is for the neonatal team to do a full physical assessment every four hours for the next twenty-four hours. You can ask to see the nurse's checklist at each turn to verify the checks were done.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know about any checklists. I just want to know why this happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It happened because I misread the tracing. I'm sorry I let you and your family down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You've really let us down. I don't even know if I can trust anything you say now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize that trust is broken. I will be here for the next hour. Would you like me to bring the department head in here to talk with you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I want the boss. I want someone who knows what they're doing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll arrange that right now. I'll be back in ten minutes with the head of the department.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language ('check on a few other things quickly', 'I just need a moment') and attempts to leave the room while the patient is still distressed.

E.justification: The error is named in the second turn, lay language is used throughout, and comprehension is checked twice ('Does that make sense so far', 'can I explain that part differently').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language multiple times and takes full personal responsibility without deflection, even under intense pushback.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('angry', 'frightening') and engages with the patient's distress, though some responses are met with a request for more than generic validation.

T.justification: The resident provides specific next steps with timelines (assessments every 4 hours for 24 hours, back in 10 minutes), a patient role (verify checks via nurse's checklist), and addresses prevention (incident report and peer review).
